title: RAW UNREVIEWED: Vitruvius lime: prior burning changes later binding while the treated material persists
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. Limestone merely pounded and mixed with sand does not cohere; after kiln treatment and slaking, the material mixes and binds as it dries. The source also distinguishes unchanged bulk from lost weight. Preserve treatment history, the same continuing material, and the later binding result.

source.layer: Historical primary work in an explicitly named translation; source content inspected, no medieval Voynich ownership implied

differentiating_relation: BURN(material) precedes WATER_CONTACT(material) and changes whether its later SAND_MIXTURE binds on drying; merely making the raw stone small is explicitly insufficient. Bulk and weight are separate properties of the treated material.
complete_source_account: II.5.1 distinguishes hard close-grained and porous source stone by structural or stucco use, with sand-dependent mixing ratios and a burnt-brick addition.
II.5.2 rejects raw crushed limestone as a binding substitute and supplies the kiln/open-pore/water/heat account.
II.5.3 keeps the original bulk while reporting about one-third weight loss, then gives drying and cohesion as the construction outcome.
known_counterexplanation: A grinding-only account predicts the same binding from crushed raw stone. A quantity-only account explains the change by the sand ratio while deleting the explicit prior-burn condition. Neither preserves both branches.
